summary: Astronaut Vitals is an offline web app that helps astronauts check their own health on long missions, when the link to Earth is slow or interrupted. Crew members log blood pressure, heart rate, blood glucose, body temperature, sleep, blood oxygen (SpO₂), bone-loading exercise, mood and symptoms, or simulate sensor readings. Every indicator is shown as NORMAL, WATCH or ALERT, always with an icon and text, and the transparent thresholds are shown next to it. If there is any ALERT or two WATCH indicators, a banner asks the astronaut to contact the flight surgeon on the ground. A clickable body figure shows how the brain, heart, bones, immune system and other areas are affected by the five hazards of spaceflight described by NASA's Human Research Program. Step-by-step guidance, 7-day trend charts and a CSV or PDF report make it easy to share data at the next medical conference. The app installs like a native app, works without a network, and keeps data on the device. It is a demo prototype that uses synthetic data, not a medical device. Demo video (27 s): https://mirasdunenbaev1305-web.github.io/NASA-Space-Apps-Astronaut-Health-Monitor/demo/ · Slides (7): https://mirasdunenbaev1305-web.github.io/NASA-Space-Apps-Astronaut-Health-Monitor/slides/
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Astronaut Vitals turns daily self-measurements into a clear, visual answer to "Am I okay, and what should I do next?" Astronauts log blood pressure, heart rate, blood glucose, body temperature, sleep, a 1-5 mood scale and symptoms (or use "Simulate readings" in place of sensors). A transparent rule engine rates each indicator NORMAL / WATCH / ALERT using editable thresholds. Any ALERT, or two or more WATCH indicators, shows "Contact flight surgeon on the ground" with the reason. A clickable body figure (brain, mood, immune system, lungs, heart, digestive system, bones) shows each area's function, related readings, spaceflight hazards and a tip. Users also get step-by-step guidance, a hazard map, trend charts with the normal band, a history table, CSV export and a printable PDF report. "Load demo week" tells a 7-day story: sleep falls from 8 h to 4.5 h, heart rate rises from 64 to 112 bpm, and status moves from NORMAL to ALERT.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

On long missions to the Moon or Mars, crews cannot always reach doctors on Earth in real time. The app supports earlier self-detection of problems, less routine load on ground teams, and a clean report ready for when the link returns. It is a Progressive Web App: it installs on a laptop or tablet and works fully offline. Data never leaves the device - no login, no backend, no tracking.

TOOLS

HTML, CSS and vanilla JavaScript (ES modules), no build step; Chart.js for trends; inline SVG for the body figure; a service worker and web manifest for offline use and installation; browser localStorage; 38 automated tests on the Node.js test runner; GitHub and GitHub Pages; VS Code and Google Chrome; AI assistants (see SI section).

CREATIVITY

Abstract numbers become a body map: the user sees which organ needs attention and why, linked to NASA's five hazards of human spaceflight. The "distance from Earth" hazard directly shaped the offline-first design and the flight-surgeon escalation.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

Accessibility: status is never shown by color alone, keyboard navigation, reduced-motion support, works on 375 px phones. Safety: clearly labeled "Demo prototype, not a medical device"; decisions stay with flight surgeons. Privacy: data stays on the device. Robustness: input validation, recovery from corrupted storage, CSV formula-injection protection. Data honesty: thresholds are simplified demo bands, not NASA flight rules; all data is synthetic.
